focus_areas.why_priority: Most recent, personally architected system with specific model names (Veo-3, Google ADK), architecture decisions (seed d
focus_areas.opener: At Filmora, your seed-based pipeline claims 40% token reduction — but prompt steering still requires LLM calls. Where exactly are the tokens you eliminated, and what replaced them?

dimensions.label: Seed Diffusion Regeneration with Targeted Prompt Steering
dimensions.resume_anchor: Leveraged seed diffusion for regeneration with targeted prompt steering to deliver real-time AI editing functionality with character identity, scene geometry, and narrative coherence across edits.
dimensions.surface: In your pipeline, when the same seed produced visually inconsistent frames across two consecutive edits, what variable changed between those two calls?
dimensions.mechanism: Your pipeline claims to preserve character identity and scene geometry across prompt-steered edits — what in the seed-regeneration mechanism actually enforces that consistency, and where does it break down under aggressive prompt changes?
dimensions.boundary: When targeted prompt steering caused semantic drift in a frame segment you intended to leave unchanged, how did you detect it, and what did you adjust in the conditioning to isolate the edit?

dimensions.label: ML Feature-Map Control for Orthogonal Editing Axes
dimensions.resume_anchor: Engineered a ML feature-map control system that translates orthogonal control axes (exposure, lighting tone, motion energy, transition speed, color palette, etc.) into pixel-level semantic generation instructions for Google Veo 3 seed-regeneration, enabling targeted edits to specific video frame segments without disturbing the video manifold.
dimensions.surface: Your feature-map system treats exposure and motion energy as orthogonal axes — in practice, what happened when an edit to one of those axes produced an unintended response in another?
dimensions.mechanism: Translating a slider value for 'motion energy' into a pixel-level semantic instruction for Veo 3 requires some intermediate representation — what is that representation and how did you validate it was actually controlling the right feature in the generated output?
dimensions.boundary: Your claim is that targeted edits don't disturb the video manifold — what does 'disturbing the manifold' look like in the actual output, and how did you decide your feature-map boundaries were tight enough to prevent it?

dimensions.label: Semantic UI-to-Latent Translation for Diffusion Conditioning
dimensions.resume_anchor: Built a semantic UI-to-latent translation interface that maps intuitive editing controls (sliders, palettes, tone adjustments) to diffusion conditioning prompt signals enabling non-technical users to perform controlled semantic AI-video regeneration while minimizing token-heavy LLM orchestration.
dimensions.surface: Your UI-to-latent interface maps a tone adjustment slider to a diffusion conditioning prompt signal — what does that mapping actually look like at the point where the slider value becomes a conditioning input?
dimensions.mechanism: You claim this interface minimizes token-heavy LLM orchestration — what orchestration did you replace and what handles the semantic translation instead, specifically for a control like color palette?
dimensions.boundary: When a user's slider combination produced a conditioning signal that conflicted with the seed's existing latent structure, what failure did you observe and how did you resolve the ambiguity in the translation layer?

dimensions.label: Cost and Token Overhead Reduction vs Veo-3 Baseline
dimensions.resume_anchor: Reduced API token overhead by ~40% and per-generation cost by ~35% versus full Veo-3 resampling (~30–50% savings at the $0.40/sec baseline).
dimensions.surface: Your 40% token reduction is measured against full Veo-3 resampling — across how many generation calls did you measure that, and what was the variance in savings across different edit types?
dimensions.mechanism: The $0.40/sec baseline applies to full Veo-3 generation — when your seed-regeneration approach only modifies a partial frame segment, what determines the actual billable duration and how did that drive your 35% cost figure?
dimensions.boundary: Your savings range is 30–50% — what edit scenarios landed at the low end of that range and what does that tell you about where the seed-regeneration approach breaks down economically?

recovery.short_answer: You mentioned the seed-regeneration workflow — take the specific moment when a prompt-steered edit landed wrong. What did the output look like and what was your next move?
recovery.honest_gap: That's fair — tell me what part of the seed-diffusion pipeline you do own end-to-end, and walk me through one concrete decision you made in that piece.
recovery.claim_conflict: Your resume says character identity is preserved across edits, but your answer suggests the seed alone doesn't enforce that — what actually maintains identity continuity in your implementation?
recovery.metric_risk: The 40% token reduction is a strong claim — walk me through exactly what you counted as a token, what the baseline call looked like, and how you measured the reduction across different edit scenarios.
recovery.overclaim_risk: You used 'video manifold' to describe what your feature-map edits avoid disturbing — in your specific implementation, what does disturbing the manifold look like in the output and how did you detect it?
recovery.bridge: The control precision you needed here — keeping edits targeted without corrupting surrounding latent structure — is actually a constraint problem. Let's move to an environment where constraints are even harder. At Optek, you were running inference on a 700MHz DSP with 16MB NPU headroom. Walk me through how you hit that sub-10ms latency target on the TinyML Audio Classification pipeline.

candidate_q4_options: Your pipeline claims real-time AI editing — what is the actual end-to-end latency from a user slider adjustment to a regenerated frame segment being returned, and which step owns the majority of that latency?
Narrative coherence across edits is listed as a delivered outcome — name a specific edit sequence where coherence failed and what in the seed or prompt structure caused it.
You built this on Google ADK — what does ADK give you architecturally that you couldn't have achieved by calling the Veo-3 API directly, and where did ADK's abstractions get in your way?
The unified seed-based workflow is framed as an alternative to full resampling — under what conditions does your pipeline fall back to full resampling, and how does that decision get made?

focus_areas.label: TinyML Audio Classification On Constrained Edge Hardware
focus_areas.anchor_context: Full-stack TinyML pipeline on a 700 MHz DSP + 16 MB NPU achieving <10 ms latency, 200 KB footprint, 4x compression via INT8 quantization and pruning.
sub_focuses: MediaPipe + TFLite-Micro INT8 inference pipeline design
INT8 quantization and pruning for 4x model compression
custom XNCC SDK deployment and latency/footprint targets
95%+ accuracy claim on AudioSet and UrbanSound8K
resume_snippets: achieving top notch-industry standards of 95%+ classification accuracy on AudioSet, UrbanSound8K
accomplishing <10 ms latency, 200 KB runtime footprint, and 4× model compression via INT8 quantization and pruning
focus_areas.why_priority: Different technical domain (edge inference, hardware-constrained ML) with specific numeric claims on latency, footprint,
focus_areas.opener: At Optek, you claim <10 ms latency on a 700 MHz DSP — but TFLite-Micro on a DSP without NPU-native ops typically bottlenecks on the dequant layer. Where was your actual bottleneck and how did you measure it?

dimensions.label: MediaPipe float32 → TFLite-Micro INT8 handoff precision cost
dimensions.resume_anchor: integrating MediaPipe Audio for real-time feature extraction (log-Mel spectrograms, MFCCs), TensorFlow Lite-Micro INT8 for quantized inference
dimensions.surface: MediaPipe runs float32 and TFLite-Micro runs INT8 — what was the precision cost of that boundary in your accuracy measurements, and how did you decide where to quantize?
dimensions.mechanism: Your log-Mel spectrograms enter the INT8 graph after quantization — what scale and zero-point did you use for that input tensor, and how did miscalibration there manifest in your classification output?
dimensions.boundary: On the 700 MHz DSP, the float32-to-INT8 conversion at the MediaPipe boundary has a runtime cost. How did you account for that conversion overhead in your <10 ms latency budget, and what did it measure in isolation?

dimensions.label: INT8 quantization and pruning for 4x model compression
dimensions.resume_anchor: 4× model compression via INT8 quantization and pruning for scalable, low-power, low latency AI application
dimensions.surface: Your 4x compression combined INT8 quantization and pruning — which of those two contributed more to the compression ratio, and how did you measure each contribution separately?
dimensions.mechanism: Pruning before quantization versus quantization before pruning produces different accuracy-compression trade-offs — in your pipeline, which order did you apply them and what happened to your accuracy curve at the 4x target?
dimensions.boundary: On a 700 MHz DSP with a 16 MB NPU, sparse weights from pruning don't always accelerate unless the hardware supports sparse execution. How did your pruned model actually run on the XNCC hardware, and did sparsity translate to measurable latency reduction?

dimensions.label: Custom XNCC SDK deployment and <10 ms / 200 KB targets
dimensions.resume_anchor: delivered a custom classifier for a 700 MHz DSP + 16 MB NPU in the proprietary XNCC development environment, accomplishing <10 ms latency, 200 KB runtime footprint
dimensions.surface: Your 200 KB footprint target on the XNCC environment — what does that 200 KB include: weights only, or weights plus activations plus runtime overhead?
dimensions.mechanism: The XNCC environment is proprietary — when TFLite-Micro ops weren't natively supported by the XNCC SDK, how did you handle the op resolution gap, and did any op fall back to a slower path that affected your latency number?
dimensions.boundary: You hit <10 ms on a 700 MHz DSP — walk me through how you profiled per-layer latency inside the XNCC environment specifically, and which layer was last to come under budget.

dimensions.label: 95%+ accuracy claim on AudioSet and UrbanSound8K
dimensions.resume_anchor: achieving top notch-industry standards of 95%+ classification accuracy on AudioSet, UrbanSound8K
dimensions.surface: AudioSet is a multilabel dataset — when you report 95%+ accuracy, what metric definition are you using: per-class mAP, top-1, something else, and why does that choice matter for AudioSet specifically?
dimensions.mechanism: UrbanSound8K has a prescribed 10-fold cross-validation split to prevent environmental leakage across recording locations — how did your evaluation protocol handle that, and what accuracy drop did you see when you enforced fold boundaries correctly?
dimensions.boundary: Your model runs INT8 on a 700 MHz DSP — but the 95%+ accuracy figure presumably came from a full-precision evaluation. What was the quantized model's accuracy on the same test set, and how large was the accuracy gap after INT8 conversion?

recovery.short_answer: Let's make it concrete — in your XNCC deployment, name one layer by type and tell me what its measured latency was on the 700 MHz DSP.
recovery.honest_gap: Fair enough — set that aside. In the parts of this pipeline you do own deeply, where did you make a technical decision that surprised you with its downstream effect on either latency or accuracy?
recovery.claim_conflict: Your resume says <10 ms and 200 KB on the XNCC hardware, but what you just described would exceed either that latency or that footprint — help me reconcile which number held and what you traded to get there.
recovery.metric_risk: That 95% figure — what was the test set size, was it held out from your quantization calibration data, and are you reporting per-class average or overall instance accuracy?
recovery.overclaim_risk: You used the term 'INT8 quantization' — in your specific XNCC pipeline, walk me through what tensor gets quantized at which step and what the scale factor was computed from.
recovery.bridge: The constraint work at Optek was about working within hard hardware limits where every byte and every millisecond had a cost. The Multimodal Bird-SQL Benchmark Construction pushed in a completely different direction — scale and ambiguity rather than constraint. Let's go there next.

candidate_q4_options: Your pipeline achieves 200 KB runtime footprint — if the XNCC environment required you to reduce that by another 30%, which component would you cut first and what accuracy risk does that carry?

You used Edge Impulse for SDK deployment alongside TFLite-Micro — at what point in your pipeline did Edge Impulse's generated SDK take over from your TFLite-Micro inference code, and why did you use both rather than one end-to-end?

Your <10 ms latency claim is on a 700 MHz DSP — how does that latency change under worst-case audio input conditions, such as high-noise frames that trigger deeper classification paths, and did you test that boundary?

INT8 quantization on MFCCs introduces rounding error that compounds across mel filterbank channels — how did you validate that your quantized feature representation was still discriminative enough to separate acoustically similar classes in your target application?

focus_areas.label: Multimodal Bird-Sql Benchmark Construction
focus_areas.anchor_context: Reconstructed BIRD-SQL benchmark (12,751+ question-SQL pairs, 95+ databases) with vision+NLP annotation and schema-aware prompt engineering for VLM evaluation.
sub_focuses: relational DB schema design for complex hybrid SQL reasoning
schema-aware prompt engineering and OCR validation for multimodal annotation
resume_snippets: Reconstructed an advanced multi-modal benchmark framework that pioneered BIRD-SQL dataset (12,751+ question-SQL pairs, 95+ large databases)
Designed relational DB schemas, and created complex hybrid SQL queries to introduce reasoning challenges for vision-language models
focus_areas.why_priority: Introduces a distinct technical territory (VLM benchmarking, SQL schema design, multimodal annotation) at a named multi-
focus_areas.opener: The original BIRD-SQL is text-only — your version adds vision annotation. For a specific query type, what failure mode does a VLM show on your benchmark that a text-LLM wouldn't, and how did your schema design expose it?

dimensions.label: Schema Design for VLM Reasoning Challenges
dimensions.resume_anchor: Designed relational DB schemas, and created complex hybrid SQL queries to introduce reasoning challenges for vision-language models
dimensions.surface: In the 95+ databases you worked with, what structural property of a relational schema made a hybrid SQL query harder for a VLM to reason over than a plain text-LLM?
dimensions.mechanism: When you designed a schema specifically to stress-test VLM cross-modal alignment, what relationship between the visual input and the table structure forced the model to fail in a way that was attributable to schema design rather than query complexity alone?
dimensions.boundary: Walk me through one schema decision you made — a specific join structure, foreign key relationship, or table cardinality choice — where you had to revise it because your evaluation protocol revealed the failure mode was ambiguous rather than schema-induced.

dimensions.label: Vision + NLP Annotation for 12,751+ Pairs
dimensions.resume_anchor: integrating vision + NLP annotation for advance database queries and designing evaluation protocols to identify model failure points
dimensions.surface: Across the 12,751+ question-SQL pairs, when a single question-SQL pair required both a visual input and a natural language annotation, what determined which modality carried the ground-truth signal for evaluation?
dimensions.mechanism: When a VLM produced an SQL answer that was syntactically valid and semantically matched the text annotation but failed against the visual input, how did your evaluation protocol surface that as a distinct failure type rather than a scoring tie?
dimensions.boundary: In the 12,751+ pairs, what breakdown in the annotation process forced you to revise the evaluation protocol — not the model results, but the protocol itself — and what did that revision change about how failure points were counted?

dimensions.label: OCR Validation in Multimodal Annotation Pipeline
dimensions.resume_anchor: OCR validation, annotating complex multimodal inputs
dimensions.surface: In the databases where OCR validation was part of your annotation pipeline, what specific class of extraction error — across those 95+ databases — occurred frequently enough that you built a validation step around it rather than handling it case by case?
dimensions.mechanism: When OCR output for a visual table cell conflicted with the corresponding SQL ground-truth annotation, what rule determined whether the annotation was corrected, the OCR was flagged, or the pair was excluded from the benchmark entirely?
dimensions.boundary: Describe a case where OCR validation passed — the extracted text matched the expected value — but the resulting question-SQL pair still introduced a reasoning artifact that distorted model evaluation, and how you detected it.

dimensions.label: Schema-Aware Prompt Engineering for VLM Evaluation
dimensions.resume_anchor: schema-aware prompt engineering, OCR validation, annotating complex multimodal inputs
dimensions.surface: When you constructed a schema-aware prompt for a VLM over one of your 95+ databases, what schema information changed the model's SQL output in a measurable way — and how did you confirm the change was schema-driven rather than prompt-length-driven?
dimensions.mechanism: In your schema-aware prompting, what was the tradeoff between injecting full schema context versus a pruned version — and how did that tradeoff manifest differently for vision queries versus pure NLP queries in your benchmark?
dimensions.boundary: When schema-aware prompting improved SQL accuracy for one query class but degraded it for another within the same database, what did that tell you about the model's internal handling of schema context, and how did you encode that asymmetry into your evaluation protocol?

strengths: All three openers force an immediate analytical position with a specific causal challenge rather than requesting a narrative — the token-elimination question, the dequant bottleneck question, and the cross-modal failure question are all hypothesis-style.

issues: Focus 1 dimension 'cost_and_token_overhead_reduction' surface probe ('across how many generation calls did you measure that') is answerable by someone who ran a single benchmark script — it does not force causal ownership of the measurement methodology.

Focus 2 dimension 'audioset_urbanSound_accuracy_validity' is partially answerable from AudioSet documentation: the mAP vs top-1 distinction and the UrbanSound8K fold structure are both public knowledge, weakening the surface and mechanism probes as ownership signals.

Focus 3 has only two declared sub_focuses but four dimensions — the OCR validation dimension (signal_weight 2.0) is the weakest area-wide: the boundary probe ('OCR passed but introduced a reasoning artifact') could be constructed theoretically without having run the pipeline.
repair_instructions: Focus 1 'cost_and_token_overhead_reduction' surface probe: replace 'across how many generation calls' with a causal challenge — e.g. 'Your 40% figure assumes a specific baseline call structure — what did one full-resampling API call cost in tokens and seconds, and what did your seed-regeneration call cost on the same edit, measured at the API response level?' This forces the candidate to name actual call structure, not a count.

Focus 2 'audioset_urbanSound_accuracy_validity' mechanism probe: replace the UrbanSound8K fold question (public knowledge) with a hands-on ownership probe — e.g. 'After INT8 conversion, you re-ran evaluation on the same test set — what was the per-class accuracy drop on your two hardest classes, and which class showed the largest delta?' This is unanswerable without having run the quantized eval.

Focus 3 'ocr_validation_multimodal_annotation' boundary probe: ground it in a specific artifact — e.g. 'Name one database from the 95+ where OCR failure was systematic enough to require a pipeline change, describe what the extraction error looked like, and what the revised validation rule was.' Generic reasoning-artifact framing allows a theoretical answer; naming a specific database forces ownership.

Focus 3 bridge in recovery currently routes back to Optek and Filmora interchangeably — since this is the third area, the bridge should either close the interview or explicitly name a cross-cutting theme (e.g. 'structured ambiguity at scale appeared in the benchmark and in the latent-space translation at Filmora — let's close on how you reason about evaluation validity when ground truth itself is noisy').
